country.name: Indonesia
country.kicker: An ocean of islands. A shared national idea.

overview.summary: A vast archipelago between the Indian and Pacific oceans. Indonesia brings many languages, landscapes, and communities into one republic. Its scale and extraordinary biodiversity make it much more than a collection of holiday islands.
overview.geography: Sumatra lies beside the Malacca Strait. Java stretches to its southeast, while Kalimantan occupies much of Borneo. Other islands extend eastward toward New Guinea and the Pacific.

whyItMatters.title: A regional center of gravity
whyItMatters.text: Southeast Asia’s largest economy has a large domestic market and an important voice in regional cooperation.

whyItMatters.title: Living systems across land and sea
whyItMatters.text: Tropical forests, reefs, and coastal ecosystems make its environmental choices consequential well beyond its islands.

stories.question: How do thousands of islands become one country?
stories.summary: The water between the islands is part of the story, not an empty gap.

sections.title: Connections across water
sections.text: Travel and trade have long linked different islands. Today, an archipelago still depends on connections between its parts. Distances and sea crossings shape the practical work of moving people and goods.

sections.title: A shared political project
sections.text: Independence was proclaimed in 1945 after Dutch colonial rule and Japanese wartime occupation. A national language and shared institutions helped build a republic across communities with very different local histories.

stories.takeaway: Indonesia is a national project spanning islands, not an island with a single identity.

stories.question: Why does one shared language matter so much?
stories.summary: Indonesian creates a meeting place across many local languages.

sections.title: A language for a common future
sections.text: The 1928 Youth Pledge made a shared language part of the independence movement’s national vision. Indonesian later became the official language of the republic.

sections.title: Unity without sameness
sections.text: Indonesian is used across the country, while regional languages remain part of everyday life. Speaking to the nation and speaking within a local community need not mean using the same language.

stories.takeaway: A shared language can connect communities without describing everything about them.

scene.mapNote: One national language connects communities spread across the archipelago.

stories.question: Why is its natural world so varied?
stories.summary: An island chain can hold many different living worlds.

sections.title: Between two biological regions
sections.text: Indonesia spans the Indomalayan and Australasian biogeographic regions. Its forests, coasts, and seas support extraordinary biodiversity, including species found nowhere else.

sections.title: Nature and everyday life
sections.text: These ecosystems support livelihoods as well as wildlife. Land use, pollution, and pressure on coastal environments affect people who depend on them. The country also sits in a region of active tectonics, where natural hazards shape life.

stories.takeaway: The same country can contain several ecological worlds, each with its own pressures.
